M301 Cooling System Inspection

Purpose:
Provide a standard procedure for inspecting the cooling
system of M301 when abnormal temperature is detected.

Applicable Machine:
M301 — CNC Machine

Trigger conditions:
● High-temperature warning

● Abnormal temperature increase

● Reduced cooling performance

● Repeated temperature alarms

Safety precautions:
1. Stop the machine according to the approved shutdown
procedure.
2. Isolate power before physical inspection.
3. Allow hot components to cool before inspection.
4. Wear required PPE.
5. Do not bypass temperature or safety sensors.

Inspection procedure:

Inspection procedure:
1. Check the coolant level.
2. Check coolant flow.
3. Inspect the cooling lines for blockage or leakage.
4. Inspect the cooling filter.
5. Check the cooling unit/fan.
6. Check the temperature sensor.
7. Record the observed temperature and condition.
8. Escalate to maintenance if the abnormal condition
persists.

Possible findings:
● Low coolant level

● Blocked filter

● Restricted coolant flow

● Cooling-system malfunction

● Sensor abnormality

Required action:
If overheating continues after basic inspection, stop
operation and request maintenance inspection

M301 Overheating Response

Purpose:
Define the procedure to follow when M301 exceeds its
normal operating temperature.

Trigger:
High-temperature alarm or abnormal temperature reading.

Procedure:
1. Stop or pause the machine safely.
2. Record the temperature and time.
3. Check the active alarm.
4. Check coolant level and flow.
5. Inspect for visible leakage or blockage.
6. Do not restart repeatedly if overheating continues.
7. Contact the maintenance team.
8. Record the incident in the maintenance log.

Escalation condition:
Repeated overheating or unresolved temperature
abnormality requires maintenance inspection before

Important:
This SOP does not authorize an operator to perform

CNC Machine Troubleshooting

Purpose:
Provide general troubleshooting guidance for CNC machine
abnormalities.

Applicable Machines:
M101, M201, M301, M401 and equivalent CNC machines.

Common symptoms:
● Overheating

● Unexpected shutdown

● Abnormal vibration

● Unusual noise

● Reduced production output

● Repeated alarms

Initial checks:
1. Identify the machine alarm.
2. Record the time and operating shift.
3. Check the machine status.
4. Check relevant operating parameters.
5. Check whether the problem has occurred previously.
6. Refer to the appropriate machine-specific SOP.
7. Escalate unresolved issues to maintenance.

Quality Inspection Procedure

Purpose:
Define the standard procedure for identifying and
recording production defects.

Applicable:
All production lines.

Inspection information:
● Product

● Production line

● Machine

● Quantity inspected

● Quantity rejected

● Defect type

● Shift

● Date

Procedure:
1. Inspect the produced components according to the
applicable quality standard.
2. Separate defective components.
3. Record the rejected quantity.
4. Classify the defect.
5. Identify the production line and machine where
applicable.
6. Notify the responsible supervisor when rejection
exceeds the accepted threshold.

A sudden increase in rejection should be investigated

Daily Machine Maintenance Checklist

Purpose:
Provide a routine checklist for identifying machine
issues before they cause production disruption.

Applicable:
Production machines.

Daily checks
● Machine cleanliness

● Coolant level

● Cooling-system condition

● Visible leakage

● Abnormal noise

● Abnormal vibration

● Temperature indicators

● Safety systems

● Machine alarms

● Lubrication condition

Recording:
The maintenance/operator record should include:
● Date

● Machine ID

● Shift

● Observed condition

● Action taken

● Status

Escalation:

Any abnormal condition that could affect safety, machine
operation, or product quality should be reported to the
appropriate maintenance/supervisory personnel.
